data.title: Pinterest Amends Executive Severance and Equity Arrangements
data.description:
Pinterest ( (PINS) ) has shared an announcement.

On November 18, 2026, Pinterest’s Talent Development and Compensation Committee further amended and restated the Severance and Change in Control Plan for employees in Level 21 positions. Subject to a participant signing a separation and release agreement and continuing to comply with confidentiality and invention-assignment terms, outstanding PSUs will vest at the greater of target or actual performance measured at a change in control in specified termination or award non-assumption circumstances.

The plan also states that equity and annual-bonus treatment applies notwithstanding contrary award or program provisions, clarifies awards when no plan benefits apply, and treats certain executives as participants solely for bonus and PSU provisions. The Committee also approved amended and restated agreements for CEO William Ready and Chief Legal and Business Affairs Officer and Corporate Secretary Wanji Walcott, entitling them to annual bonus payments and PSU treatment under the plan, subject to its terms.

The agreements provided that more favorable definitions of “cause” and “good reason” would apply, while Ready’s agreement treated a resignation for good reason outside a change in control as a termination without cause for annual-bonus purposes. The Committee also amended Ready’s PSU awards so, subject to a release, such a resignation would receive the same treatment as a termination without cause, with a prorated portion remaining eligible to vest based on actual performance through the applicable performance period.

data.description:

On November 19, 2026, Kairos Pharma’s Compensation Committee approved an aggregate of 816,335 restricted stock units for certain executive officers under its 2023 Equity Incentive Plan. John S. Yu received 400,000, Neil Bhomick 200,000, Ramachandran Murali 16,335 and Doug Samuelson 200,000; each unit represented the right to receive one common share upon vesting and vested immediately upon issuance.

data.title: Kiwi Property Earnings Call Highlights Growth and Risks
data.description:
Kiwi Property Group ((NZ:KPG)) has held its Q2 earnings call. Read on for the main highlights of the call.

Kiwi Property Group delivered a predominantly positive earnings call, supported by strong occupancy, leasing spreads, customer visits, like-for-like rental income and lower gearing. However, reported AFFO and net rental income fell after asset sales, while modest portfolio sales growth, Vero Centre vacancies and Drury and ANZ Raranga valuation reductions remained challenges.

Retail-Led Strategy Gains Momentum

Kiwi Property said its refreshed strategy is progressing, with retail-led assets now representing 74% of portfolio value, up from 54% at half year 2022. Office assets fell 11% and other assets declined 12%, leaving about 95% of the portfolio concentrated in Auckland and Hamilton.

Customer Visits Rise Above Pre-COVID Levels

Annual customer visits reached 37.3 million, an increase of 3.8%, or 1.4 million visits, from the prior year. Portfolio sales rose 2% to $1.9 billion, although first-half sales growth of 1.5% remained modest against a difficult consumer backdrop.

Retail Occupancy Remains Strong

Portfolio occupancy was 97.9%, rising to 98.7% on a pro forma basis after a nearby Sylvia Park property was leased. Retail-led occupancy reached 99.4%, rental growth was 4.1% and leasing spreads were 3.9%, with about 65% of income linked to fixed or CPI-based reviews.

Underlying Earnings Improve

Reported AFFO was affected by recent divestments, but like-for-like AFFO rose 1.5% to $48.7 million when those impacts were excluded. Like-for-like net rental income increased 4.8% to $88.6 million, helped by Sylvia Park, Resido and $1.5 million in Vero Centre surrender fees.

Net Profit Benefits From Lower Costs

Net profit after tax increased to $36.3 million from $9.8 million, mainly because fair value losses on investment properties were lower and interest-rate swap values improved. Net finance expenses fell $5.3 million after debt repayment from asset sales, while employment and administration costs declined by $0.8 million.

Sylvia Park Builds Customer and Tenant Momentum

Sylvia Park attracted more than 17 million visits during the year, while the IKEA Walkway drew about 1.5 million visitors from outside Auckland, up 21% since IKEA opened. Lifestyle furniture sales rose 15%, with Adidas, LEGO, Mecca and STACKS supermarket adding further tenant momentum.

Shopping Centers Post Positive Sales

All three shopping centers recorded sales growth, led by Sylvia Park at 2.8% and The Base Te Awa at 3%, while LynnMall rose 0.4%. Specialty sales increased to $12,200 per square meter from $11,600, and occupancy costs fell to 15.3%, below the 17% to 18% target range.

Leasing Strength Supports Income

New leasing was particularly strong at The Base, where spreads rose 15.2%, and Vero Centre, where spreads increased 8.9%. Rent reviews added 4.2% growth, while retail-led occupancy has stayed around 99% or higher for eight years and the weighted average lease expiry was 3.5 years.

Portfolio Value and Gearing Improve

The portfolio was valued at $3 billion, with the capitalization rate steady at 6.28% and net tangible assets at $1.11 per share. Excluding ASB North Wharf, value increased $28.7 million to $3.04 billion, while gearing fell to 34.4% from 37.4% after the sale.

Refinancing Strengthens the Balance Sheet

Kiwi Property refinanced $900 million of bank debt at low margins, extending average drawn debt maturity from 2.9 to 3.5 years without a material increase in borrowing costs. It also issued a $200 million seven-year green bond, with 78% of drawn debt fixed at 3.61% and liquidity headroom of $245 million.

Green-Rated Assets Expand

Green-rated assets reached $2.2 billion, or 73% of portfolio value, with Sylvia Park and ANZ Raranga receiving six-star NABERSNZ ratings and The Base Te Awa receiving five stars. Overall, 54% of the portfolio carried a rating of 5.5 stars or better, while shopping centers were added to the sustainable debt framework.

Sylvia Green Redevelopment Advances

The $19 million Sylvia Green project carries a targeted internal rate of return of 10% and a 7% yield on cost. It will add about 1,500 square meters of leased space, expand Kmart by roughly 1,400 square meters and create a new plaza, green space, seating, food offerings and digital media facilities.

Vero Centre Refresh Receives Positive Feedback

The Vero Centre redevelopment includes a digital art display, redesigned entrances, a refurbished lobby and cafe, and a new end-of-trip facility. Management said tenants had responded positively and were making good use of the upgraded amenities.

Drury Stage One Remains on Program

Civil works at Drury Stage 1 remain scheduled for completion in 2027, with external road upgrades expected to begin during the summer. The new train station opened in August with park-and-ride facilities, while agreed land sales reached about $115 million and discussions continued on another 2.6-hectare retail site.

Drury Stage Two Offers Longer-Term Potential

Drury Stage 2 has more than 150,000 square meters of approved gross floor area across retail, office, hotel, residential and community uses. Management estimates remaining capital expenditure at about $159 million, completed value at $376 million and the target internal rate of return at 15% or more, while stressing that these figures are indicative.

Future Retail and Office Opportunities

Kiwi Property is assessing expansion at Sylvia Park, LynnMall and The Base, alongside mixed-use projects and a possible third Sylvia Park office building. A potential office development near ANZ Raranga could cover 5,000 to 6,000 square meters, with management seeking at least 50% pre-leasing before seeking approval.

Employee Engagement and AI Adoption

Employee engagement was measured at 77%, placing Kiwi Property in the upper quartile of comparable businesses. Management also said 82% of software license users had made Copilot a daily habit, highlighting the company’s focus on productivity and technology adoption.

Reported AFFO Falls After Divestments

Reported AFFO declined $3.3 million, or 6.4%, to $48.6 million, while AFFO per share fell 7.3% to $0.0294. Management attributed the drop mainly to the divestments of The Plaza and ASB North Wharf, noting that like-for-like AFFO increased when those assets were excluded.

Reported Rental Income Also Declines

Reported net rental income fell 10.9% after the disposals of The Plaza and ASB North Wharf. On a like-for-like basis, however, net rental income rose 4.8%, reflecting stronger performance from the remaining portfolio.

Consumers Remain Under Pressure

Management described the six-month period as difficult for consumers, with higher fuel costs adding pressure to household budgets. Executives said Kiwi Property’s sales performance reflected the current state of the New Zealand economy, helping explain the slower growth rate.

Portfolio Sales Growth Is Modest

Total portfolio sales increased $37 million, or 2%, in the 12 months to September 30. Management acknowledged that this growth was below a stronger comparison cited during the question-and-answer session, underscoring the cautious retail environment.

Drury Stage One Takes an Impairment

Drury Stage 1 incurred $10.2 million of costs during the half, including capitalized interest. Because the increase in value was below the costs incurred, Kiwi Property recognized a $5.7 million impairment, mainly reflecting revised assumptions about the timing of future development costs.

Drury Stage Two Value Falls

Drury Stage 2 recorded a $5.2 million fair value decline. Management said the land remains several years from development and is therefore more exposed to subdued land market conditions.

Vero Centre Leasing Remains Slow

About two floors at Vero Centre are vacant, including space on Level 15. Management said demand exists, but leasing activity has moved slowly, while additional non-retail vacancies emerged in commercial and industrial sites near Sylvia Park.

One-Off Tax Charge Lifts Expense

Current tax expense was $6.9 million higher, largely because of a one-off depreciation recovery tax charge linked to ASB North Wharf. Management said the charge was excluded from AFFO, limiting its impact on the company’s underlying earnings measure.

ANZ Raranga Valuation Reduced

ANZ Raranga’s value declined $4.4 million after forecast capital spending increased for replacement air-conditioning units. The reduction added to the valuation pressures recorded across selected development and office assets.

Cost Focus Continues

Full-time equivalent employees fell to 133 from a peak of about 165, representing a workforce reduction of roughly 12% over that period. Management said it remained focused on removing costs while maintaining the capability needed to operate and develop the portfolio.

Guidance Points to Higher Dividends and Development Activity

Kiwi Property confirmed FY27 dividend guidance of $0.0575 per share, up 2.7% on FY26 and expected to sit at the higher end of the 90% to 100% AFFO payout range. Management is targeting average annual dividend growth of 3%, while Drury Stage 1 remains scheduled for 2027, land-sale proceeds are expected in FY28 and FY29, and potential Sylvia Park and office projects remain subject to pre-leasing and Board approval.

Kiwi Property’s call showed a stronger underlying business beneath the headline earnings decline caused by asset sales. High occupancy, improving like-for-like income, disciplined financing and a higher dividend outlook were key positives, while consumer pressure, slower Vero Centre leasing and development-related valuation risks remain important issues for investors.

data.title: Texas Pacific Land Announces $3 Billion EagleRock Land Merger
data.description:
Texas Pacific Land ( (TPL) ) has issued an update.

On November 23, 2026, TPL announced it had entered a merger agreement dated November 22, 2026, to acquire EagleRock Land and its operating subsidiary in an all-stock transaction with an implied equity value of approximately $3.0 billion. The deal used a new holding company, New TPL, which would be renamed Texas Pacific Land Corporation at closing.

TPL shareholders would retain one New TPL share for each TPL share, while EagleRock Class A holders and Opco unitholders would receive 0.0831 New TPL shares per eligible interest; paired Class B shares would be canceled. The announced terms provided for approximately 86% ownership by existing TPL shareholders and 14% ownership by EagleRock equityholders at closing.

The release described a combined footprint of approximately 1.0 million fee-owned surface acres and 105,000 dedicated water-solutions acres. The transaction brought together TPL’s surface acreage, oil and gas royalty interests, water solutions and land commercialization expertise with EagleRock’s acreage, water infrastructure and operator relationships in the Permian Basin.

Completion remained subject to EagleRock shareholder approval, regulatory clearances, an effective SEC registration statement and NYSE and NYSE Texas listing authorization, among other customary conditions. No TPL shareholder vote was required, while holders representing approximately 63% of EagleRock voting power signed support agreements backing the transaction.

On November 22, 2026, TPL’s board approved an additional $500.0 million under its stock repurchase authorization, leaving approximately $670.2 million available. The company said repurchases were funded by cash from operations and could be conducted through open-market, privately negotiated or other transactions, subject to market conditions and legal requirements.

data.title: BGSF Receives NYSE Non-Compliance Notice Over Listing Standards
data.description:
BGSF ( (BGSF) ) has provided an announcement.

On November 23, 2026, BGSF announced that it had received a non-compliance letter from the New York Stock Exchange on November 17. The company’s 30-trading-day average market capitalization was approximately $45.0 million, below the $50 million requirement, while its last reported stockholders’ equity was approximately $46.4 million, also below the threshold.

Under NYSE procedures, BGSF said it intended to notify the exchange within 10 business days and was required to submit a business plan within 45 calendar days, showing how it would regain compliance within 18 months. The non-compliance had no immediate effect on the company’s common-stock listing, which was subject to the NYSE’s acceptance of the plan and quarterly monitoring during the cure period.

data.title: Tuya Reports Third-Quarter 2026 Results, Declares Cash Dividend
data.description:
The latest update is out from Tuya ( (TUYA) ).

Tuya Inc. is a global AI cloud platform service provider whose offerings include platform-as-a-service, AI applications and other services, and smart home and robot products.

On Nov. 23, 2026, Tuya reported unaudited third-quarter results for the period ended Sept. 30, 2026, with revenue of US$98.6 million, up 19.5% year over year, and net profit of US$18.5 million. PaaS revenue rose 18.3% to US$70.1 million, while the company declared a cash dividend.

Operating margin increased to 9.0% from 4.6%, although gross margin fell to 45.8% from 48.3%; operating cash generation was US$12.7 million. Premium PaaS customers reached 331 and registered AI developers exceeded 2.18 million, while AI-native category shipments grew more than 400% year over year, according to the company.
